# Downloading many runs on Longleaf {#sec-at-scale}

For more than a handful of runs, use a **SLURM array job**: one script,
run once per accession, with SLURM handing each copy a different line of
your accession list. The repository's
[`scripts/download_sra.sh`](https://github.com/jpflores-13/download-public-data/blob/main/scripts/download_sra.sh)
does this.

## What the script does, per run

```{mermaid}
flowchart LR
  A["line N of<br/>SRR_Acc_List.txt"] --> B["prefetch<br/>--max-size u"] --> C["vdb-validate"] --> D["fasterq-dump<br/>--threads 6 --temp ..."] --> E["pigz"] --> F["count reads →<br/>read_counts.tsv"] --> G["delete .sra<br/>and temp"]
```

It skips runs that already have a `.fastq.gz`, so if some tasks fail you
can resubmit the whole array and only the missing ones run.

## Running it

```bash
cd /work/users/j/d/jdoe
git clone https://github.com/jpflores-13/download-public-data.git
mkdir -p airway && cd airway
cp ../download-public-data/examples/airway_SRR_Acc_List.txt SRR_Acc_List.txt   # or your own list

mkdir -p logs
N=$(grep -c . SRR_Acc_List.txt)          # number of non-empty lines
sbatch --array=1-${N}%4 ../download-public-data/scripts/download_sra.sh SRR_Acc_List.txt fastq
```

- `--array=1-8` runs tasks 1 to 8; the **`%4`** means at most four at once.
  Keep this low (2–6). Many simultaneous downloads don't go faster, they
  overload the shared filesystem, and NCBI may throttle you.
- Arguments: the accession list, and the output folder.
- `logs/` must exist before submitting; SLURM won't create it.

::: {.callout-note}
## Module names

The script runs `module load sratoolkit` and tries `module load pigz`. If
Longleaf's module is named differently (`module avail sra`), edit that line.
If you use conda instead, replace it with `source activate sra` (or
`conda activate sra`).
:::

## Watching it

```bash
squeue -u $USER                                   # tasks show as JOBID_1, JOBID_2, ...
tail logs/sra_download-<JOBID>_3.out              # one task's log
grep -l -i error logs/*.err                       # any task with errors
sacct -j <JOBID> --format=JobID,State,Elapsed,MaxRSS
cat fastq/read_counts.tsv                         # filled in as tasks finish
```

## Resources

The script asks for 6 CPUs, 8 GB memory and 12 hours per run. That's plenty
for typical bulk RNA-seq (20–50 M pairs). For very large runs (> 50 GB `.sra`),
raise `-t` and make sure `/work` has the space
([fasterq-dump](fasterq-dump.qmd#disk-space)).

## Without SLURM (a laptop, a workstation)

The same steps in a loop:

```bash
while read -r acc; do
  prefetch "$acc" --max-size u -O sra
  vdb-validate "sra/$acc"
  fasterq-dump "sra/$acc" --threads 4 --temp tmp --outdir fastq
  pigz -p 4 fastq/"$acc"*.fastq
  rm -rf "sra/$acc"
done < SRR_Acc_List.txt
```
